# willbuilds.ai — site guide

A static site generated from a few content files by a zero-dependency Node script. GitHub Pages serves the generated HTML straight from this repo.

## Workflow

```bash
# 1. edit something in content/
# 2. rebuild the pages
node build.mjs
# 3. preview at http://localhost:8000
python3 -m http.server 8000
# 4. commit content/ AND the generated files, then push
```

Requires Node 18+. There is nothing to install.

## Files

```
content/
  site.json        Name, intro text, About page copy, contact links, section blurbs
  projects.json    Every project — one record each (see below)
  notes/           Notes as Markdown; files starting with _ are ignored
build.mjs          Turns content/ into HTML pages
css/style.css      All styling: design tokens, light + dark theme
js/main.js         Search + tag filters on the Projects and Lab pages
images/            Screenshots

# Generated by build.mjs — never edit by hand, they are overwritten
index.html  404.html  sitemap.xml
projects/  lab/  about/  notes/
```

`build.mjs` deletes and recreates `projects/`, `lab/`, `about/` and `notes/` on every run, so don't put hand-made files in those folders.

## Sections

| Page | What goes there |
|---|---|
| **Projects** (`/projects/`) | Working software: tools, games and apps people can use or that are substantially built |
| **Lab** (`/lab/`) | Prototypes and experiments that aren't finished products yet |
| **Notes** (`/notes/`) | Writing. Hidden from the nav and homepage until the first note exists |
| **About** (`/about/`) | Who I am, plus links |

Old links still work: `willbuilds.ai/#projects` and `#about` redirect to the new pages, and `#contact` lands on the footer of any page.

## Add a project

Add a record to `content/projects.json` and run `node build.mjs`. Required fields:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `slug` | lowercase-with-dashes; becomes the URL, e.g. `/projects/my-tool/` |
| `title` | Display name |
| `category` | `projects` or `lab` |
| `status` | `live`, `in-development`, `prototype`, `experimental`, `paused` or `archived` |
| `description` | One or two sentences, shown in lists |

Optional fields — any that are missing are simply left off the page:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `featured` | `true` to show it on the homepage (up to 4) |
| `overview` | List of paragraphs for the project page |
| `problem`, `solution` | One paragraph each |
| `details` | List of bullet points |
| `tags` | Shown as `--tag`. A tag used by 2+ entries in a section becomes a filter button |
| `technologies` | Shown as "built with" |
| `thumbnail`, `thumbnailAlt` | e.g. `images/my-tool.png`; shown in lists and on the project page |
| `liveUrl`, `sourceUrl` | Buttons on the project page |

The build stops with a clear message if a required field is missing, a slug is duplicated, or a thumbnail file doesn't exist.

## Add a note

Copy `content/notes/_template.md` to `content/notes/your-slug.md`, fill in the front matter (`title`, `date`, `summary`, `tags`) and write the body in Markdown. The first note makes Notes appear in the navigation and on the homepage.

## Theme

Design tokens live at the top of `css/style.css` (`--color-*`, `--text-*`, `--space-*`). The light theme is the default; the `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block below it swaps the colors when the visitor's OS is in dark mode. Status badges pair a text label with a mark shape, so status never depends on color alone.
